tier_reason: First-party README tables compare against C libjpeg-turbo with public harnesses (benches/c_baseline.c for C decode via tj3Decompress8 with accurate DCT and fancy upsampling, benches/decode.rs, examples/bench_c_encode_linux.c and examples/bench_encode_matrix.rs). The decode table that carries the win (i5-10400, C 3.1.2) states neither rustc version nor how the C library was built, so it is C. Only the encode portable table, where Rust is slower, has full methodology (rustc 1.98.1, cc -O2 harness, official libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 .deb, AMD EPYC 7763).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Decode table: stock cargo build --release (Cargo.toml [profile.release] lto = true), runtime AVX2/SSE2 dispatch; rustc version and the C libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 build not stated. Encode portable table: rustc 1.98.1, no RUSTFLAGS, C harness compiled with cc -O2 against the official libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 .deb (perf-portable-vs-native.yml). Supplementary i5-10400 encode table: RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native.
corrections.workload: JPEG decode (TurboJPEG-style decompress to RGB, quality 75) of in-repo fixtures tests/fixtures/photo_*.jpg from 64x64 to 3840x2160 at 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 (the 640x480 4:2:0 row is gradient_640x480.jpg), and encode of the same set at 320x240 to 1920x1080; Rust vs C in microseconds per image on Intel i5-10400, AMD EPYC 7763/9V74 runners and Apple M1 Pro.
corrections.caveats: Pure-Rust reimplementation (port) of libjpeg-turbo, not an FFI binding: no C dependency, byte-for-byte cross-validated against C in CI. Under the ports rule it may fold into libjpeg-turbo (zlib-rs precedent); it is listed here because it is measured against the original. First-party harness, tiny project (9 stars); recent commits are co-authored by Claude. The x86_64 decode win (README table, i5-10400 turbo off, C 3.1.2) is 3 to 23% on most sizes but 64x64 (1.23x) and the 640x480 gradient (1.05x) lose; that table is undated and does not state rustc or the C build. An earlier report on the same CPU (experiments/x86_64_avx2_final_report.md, 2026-04-12) gives different absolute times but the same direction (0.83 to 0.98x on most cases, progressive 0.83 to 0.91x). The stock portable encoder is 1.05 to 1.10x C 3.2.0's time at 1080p on Zen 3/Zen 4 runners (slower); only the target-cpu=native i5-10400 build beats C 3.1.2 by 2 to 7%. Apple M1 Pro: decode 0.99 to 1.07x, encode 1.03 to 1.07x of C (not faster). README says no memory-safety guarantee yet (unsafe SIMD under audit) and the classic libjpeg ABI is experimental.

notes: Numbers in claimed_speedup match the README tables. It is a Rust port, not a wrapper (README: 'no FFI to a C codec'), so the duplicate question is a policy call for the orchestrator. Rust entry under a C++-filtered category: language-filter mismatch.

tier_reason: First-party numbers with public bench code (zenjpeg/benches/decode_zenbench.rs: interleaved zenbench over 10 CID22-512 photos, C reference via mozjpeg-sys FFI) and a stated CPU (Ryzen 9 7950X, WSL2) and flags (release, default target), but no rustc version (rust-toolchain.toml pins only 'stable') and no C compiler/flags for the mozjpeg-sys build, so not A. No committed result file holding the README's CID22 MiB/s figures was found.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (Ryzen 9 7950X, single-threaded, 10 CID22 512x512 photos at Q85 4:2:0): baseline decode 73.8 MiB/s with default Triangle upsampling vs libjpeg-turbo/mozjpeg 78.1 MiB/s (0.94x, slower); 80.4 MiB/s with NearestNeighbor (box) upsampling (1.03x, but that skips the fancy upsampling C performs); progressive decode 46 vs 34 MiB/s (1.35x faster), the one single-thread like-for-like win. Parallel decode with DRI (rayon, --features parallel) vs single-threaded libjpeg-turbo: 1.56 vs 3.86 ms at 1024, 3.05 vs 15.8 ms at 2048, 8.74 vs 65.3 ms at 4096 (about 2.5x, 5.2x, 7.5x, derived from page data); this compares a multi-core decode with a single-thread one. The same synthetic set run single-threaded (CLAUDE.md, 2026-02-15, commit 39f012f) gives 3.66 vs 3.86, 14.8 vs 15.8, 61.9 vs 65.3 ms (about 1.05 to 1.07x faster, derived from page data), and progressive 0.60 to 0.69x of mozjpeg's time on synthetic images.
corrections.workload: JPEG decode to RGB of 10 CID22-512 training photos (512x512) re-encoded by mozjpeg-rs at Q85 4:2:0, baseline and progressive, timed in interleaved zenbench A/B runs (zenjpeg/benches/decode_zenbench.rs). The parallel-decode table uses synthetic noise+patches images with restart markers at 1024, 2048 and 4096 px (CLAUDE.md Parallel Decode, 2026-02-15).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo bench --release, default target (no -C target-cpu=native), runtime SIMD dispatch via archmage; rust-toolchain.toml pins channel 'stable' only and the rustc version is not recorded; C reference is mozjpeg-sys 2.2 with nasm_simd, built by its build script with unstated C compiler and flags
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark; tiny project (15 stars). The C reference is mozjpeg-sys 2.2 (mozjpeg's libjpeg-turbo-derived decoder via FFI), not stock libjpeg-turbo 3.x. Single-thread baseline decode is 6% slower than C on CID22 with the default Triangle upsampling; NearestNeighbor only matches C by doing cheaper upsampling. The default decoder uses the 'Jpegli' integer IDCT, not libjpeg's ISLOW; the README says the pixel-exact Libjpeg IDCT adds about 37% overhead, so the progressive 1.35x win is measured with output that differs slightly from libjpeg-turbo (like-for-like margin unmeasured). The parallel table compares rayon multi-threaded zenjpeg with single-threaded libjpeg-turbo, against the repo's own benchmarks/README rule never to compare single-threaded and thread-pooled contenders; its libjpeg-turbo column comes from synthetic noise+patches images (Feb 2026), not CID22. The Feb 2026 synthetic single-thread table shows zenjpeg 5 to 7% faster on baseline, the newer CID22 run shows it 6% slower. rustc version not recorded. AGPL-3.0 copyleft (commercial license sold separately).

notes: Claimed numbers match README; the only genuine single-thread like-for-like win is progressive decode (1.35x, non-pixel-exact IDCT). Parallel 2.5x to 7.5x is multi-thread vs single-thread and should not be quoted as a speedup over libjpeg-turbo. Rust entry under a C++-filtered category: language-filter mismatch.

tier_reason: First-party zenbench and callgrind numbers against libwebp (via webp 0.3.1 / libwebp-sys 0.14) with no CPU model or rustc version; the project's own committed data shows zenwebp slower than libwebp in nearly every mode, and its one large 'win' (lossless m6 2.6x) is documented in its own CLAUDE.md as skipped work.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Not faster than libwebp per the project's own committed data. Lossy encode (512x512 photo, q75, zen/libwebp wall, 2026-07-16): m0 1.79x, m2 0.97x (3% faster, one image, under load), m4 1.16x, m6 1.40x slower; the README's m4 1.35x / m5 1.34x / m6 1.32x are older slowdown ratios, not speedups. Lossless encode: README 'm6 2.6x faster' (docs/PERFORMANCE.md 132 vs 340 ms, 2026-03-26) predates the 2026-07-14 fix that ported libwebp's predictor-bits search and dual no-cache refs; CLAUDE.md calls the earlier m5/m6 win 'skipped work', and benchmarks/msweep_post70_2026-07-14.tsv gives zen/lib wall geomeans of 1.18x (m2) to 1.92x (m0) and 1.39x at m6 over 11 files (derived from page data). Lossy decode: README 1.06 to 1.15x are slowdown factors (CLAUDE.md v2 table, 2026-03-27: 0.45x to 0.94x of libwebp throughput; docs/PERFORMANCE.md: 1.14 to 2.22x slower). Lossless decode: 1.23 to 1.31x slower on screenshots ('remaining lossless decode gap'); the 512x512 photo row (101 vs 107 MPix/s) is labelled '0.94x (faster)' but is about 6% slower (derived from page data).
corrections.license: AGPL-3.0 or commercial (dual-licensed); upstream image-webp code MIT OR Apache-2.0; versions 0.1.x to 0.3.x were MIT OR Apache-2.0
corrections.caveats: Rejected as not faster: the README's speed tables are stale or read in the wrong direction. Its own CLAUDE.md and benchmarks/speed_parity_2026-07-16.md show libwebp ahead in lossy encode (except m2 at 0.97x on one image), lossless encode (all methods once the m5/m6 work skipped before 2026-07-14 was ported), lossy decode (6 to 55% slower) and lossless decode on screenshots. docs/PERFORMANCE.md's lossless-decode table is internally inconsistent (MPix/s columns do not match the ratios). The search agent's README-vs-PERFORMANCE.md 'contradiction' on lossy decode is a misreading: both say zenwebp is slower; the README figures are newer, smaller slowdowns. Derived from image-rs/image-webp (not a GitHub fork). Strengths that are real: pure safe Rust (forbid(unsafe_code)), bit-exact lossy decode vs libwebp on 43,414 files, streaming decode at 1.5 MB peak vs libwebp's 34 MB. No CPU model stated; rustc version not stated. AGPL-3.0 copyleft.

notes: Reject not-faster, and the lone headline win (lossless m6 2.6x) is invalid evidence by the project's own account (it skipped libwebp's predictor-bits search and dual no-cache refs). If kept under keep-and-document, it belongs as a safe-Rust/memory-bounded codec at roughly 0.7 to 0.97x libwebp speed. Rust entry under a C++-filtered category: language-filter mismatch.
